tip: между (mezhdu = between) takes the instrumental, so дом (dom = house) becomes домами (damami = houses) in the plural.
For motion to a spot, под (pod = under) switches to the accusative: под кровать (pod kravat = under the bed).
Past active participles end in -ший: выросшие дети (vyrosshie deti = the grown-up children), from вырасти (vyrasti = to grow up).
Seasons take the bare instrumental to mean in that season, no preposition: весной (vesnoy = in spring), from весна (vesna = spring).
говорят, что (gavaryat, chto = they say that) is an impersonal 3rd-plural verb, no subject needed, reading as it is said.
с (s) plus genitive means off or from a place or event: сбежал с урока (sbezhal s uroka = ran off from class), урок (urok) going to урока.
The prefix пере- (pere-) on a motion verb means across: перелетела (pereletela = flew across) через океан (cherez akean = over the ocean).
Present active participles end in -щий: скучающий ребёнок (skuchayushchiy rebyonok = the bored child), from скучать (skuchat = to be bored).
через (cherez) plus accusative counts time from now: через полгода (cherez palgoda = in half a year), meaning after that span.
Past passive participles end in -нный and act as adjectives: сломанный стул (slomannyy stul = broken chair), from сломать (slamat = to break).
кататься на (katatsya na) plus prepositional means to go doing a sport: катаемся на лыжах (kataemsya na lyzhah = we ski).
Days of the week take в plus accusative: в четверг (v chetverg = on Thursday), четверг unchanged as an inanimate noun.
Some destinations take на plus accusative, not в (v): поехали на море (paehali na more = went to the sea).
Russian keeps the original tense in reported speech: сказал, что придёт (skazal, chto pridyot = said he will come), no backshift to would.
For a repeated trip use ходить (hadit), not one-way идти (idti): каждый день я хожу (kazhdyy den ya hazhu = every day I go).
Weeks take на plus prepositional, not в (v): на следующей неделе (na sleduyushchey nedele = next week).
After a request, чтобы takes a past-form verb: попросил, чтобы я помог (paprasil, chtoby ya pamog = asked that I help).
For an embedded yes/no question use ли after the key word: сделал ли я (sdelal li ya = whether I did), no if word needed.
из ... в ... expresses repetition: из года в год (iz goda v god = year after year), год appearing first in genitive, then accusative.
Months take в plus prepositional: в мае (v maye = in May), from май (may = May).
Past passive uses было plus a short participle: письмо было отправлено (pismo bylo atpravleno = the letter was sent).
мимо (mimo = past) takes the genitive: проехали мимо парка (praehali mimo parka = drove past the park), парк (park) becoming парка.
над (nad = over) takes the instrumental: пролетел над городом (praletel nad gorodom = flew over the city), город (gorod) becoming городом.
с plus instrumental means with: с каждым днём (s kazhdym dnyom = with each day), день (den) becoming днём.
An -я gerund shows a simultaneous action by the same subject: читая книгу (chitaya knigu = while reading a book), from читать (chitat = to read).
A negative word still needs не on the verb: никто не сказал (nikto ne skazal = nobody said), the double negative is required.
Years take в plus prepositional: в прошлом году (v proshlom gadu = last year), год (god) taking the special locative ending году.
улыбающаяся (ulybayushchayasya = smiling) is a participle used like an adjective, agreeing with женщина (zhenshchina = woman) in gender and case.
Russian always puts a comma before что (chto = that) in reported speech: сказали, что согласны (skazali, chto saglasny = said that we agree).
открытое (atkrytoe = opened) is a past passive participle used like an adjective, agreeing with окно (akno = window).
